audit.head: 5c68e54
audit.scope: workflow-authoring/workflow-testing/application/contracts/MCP bridge/v2 authoring API and v2 execution changes
audit.isolation: All scripts use in-memory SQLite, synthetic Vault passwords and schemas. No official data directory, credentials, external MCP, network endpoint or model provider accessed. Repository files were not modified; no build executed.
audit.migrationConstraint: Any repair must preserve already-delivered v1 and v2 migration DDL/checksums; use later sequential migrations only if needed.

findings.title: rowLimitArgument overwrites locked resource arguments before dispatch
findings.contract: Fixed environment/resource binding cannot be overridden by generated workflow parameters; native limits must preserve locked arguments.
findings.cause: resolveArguments applies all lockedArguments, then unconditionally writes Math.min(...) to the model-selected rowLimitArgument path. The mapping validator only checks argumentsMappings paths for lock overlap. Before-dispatch recomputation repeats the same overwrite and passes its hash check.
findings.impact: An authored workflow can route a call to a different numeric tenant/resource despite a fixed binding; a same-environment binding can still access the wrong locked resource.
findings.minimalFix: During publish validation and again before dispatch, reject rowLimitArgument paths equal to, ancestors of, or descendants of any locked argument path, using the same JSON Pointer overlap semantics. A locked limit policy must remain immutable unless a separate explicit contract permits a bounded reduction.
tests: Top-level numeric tenantId locked to 123 and rowLimitArgument=/tenantId must fail before dispatch.
Nested lock /scope and limit /scope/tenantId, lock /scope/tenantId and parent limit /scope must reject.
Legitimate independent /limit still clamps to user/workflow/binding limits; zero business calls for overlap failures.

findings.title: HTTP v2 publication omits required binding CAS when the field is absent
findings.contract: The common Authoring DTO requires expectedBindingRevisions and publication must pin the reviewed draft/capability/binding revisions for Web, MCP and Assistant.

trigger.precondition: Draft references binding rev1; binding independently changes to rev2 without changing draft revision.

observed.verificationLevel: Direct AuthoringService call with the exact body forwarded by the HTTP route; route source confirms no additional DTO validation. No live HTTP request was necessary.

findings.cause: Only Application.handle validates the fixed MCP schema. The Web route invokes AuthoringService.publish directly, and publish forwards undefined expectedBindingRevisions to Engine.publish, whose check is conditional.
findings.impact: A Web/API request can publish unreviewed binding configuration despite a stable draft revision; Web has weaker publication invariants than MCP.
findings.minimalFix: Validate the full common publish DTO at the AuthoringService boundary, require expectedBindingRevisions and expectedCapabilityRevisions on every v2 publication, and reject missing/extra/wrong-typed fields before any mutation. Keep legacy publication compatibility explicitly separate.
tests: Authenticated HTTP v2 publish without expectedBindingRevisions returns INPUT_INVALID/428 and produces no version, no command record and no draft revision increment.
Review binding rev1, mutate to rev2, publish with expected rev1 must 409; with reviewed rev2 succeeds.
Same invalid DTO rejected consistently via Web service and official MCP; v1 legacy publication regression remains passing.

findings.title: host_tool can replace the discovered output contract with an incompatible node schema
findings.contract: Host tool identity, fixed arguments and real output schema are frozen at publish; user-proposed definitions/fixtures cannot replace the actual capability contract.
findings.cause: Authoring only checks that a codex_host capability has input/output schemas; it never requires node.outputSchema to match or safely specialize cap.outputSchema. advance validates only node.outputSchema and marks the host result accepted.
findings.impact: The published real host contract is informational: incompatible data is accepted and can drive downstream mappings or reports as a successful host result.
findings.minimalFix: Derive/fill the host_tool output schema from the exact capability revision when creating nodes or require proven compatible constraints. At checkpoint/advance validate against the frozen capability output schema as well as any additional node schema. Avoid consulting mutable current capability for an existing published run.
tests: Integer capability vs string node schema must reject authoring/publish, or invalid submitted string must fail without consuming checkpoint.
Missing required fields and extra fields in host reports fail the frozen schema.
Capability changes after publication do not mutate existing frozen schemas; compatible actual host payload succeeds and remains marked host_reported.

findings.title: isolated Mock runner does not copy capability revisions, so valid host_tool cases cannot run
findings.contract: Deterministic Mock/scripted results must cover host_tool dataflow using isolated metadata; they must clearly separate synthetic execution from actual host execution.
findings.cause: The test DB gets only connection/binding schemas. Engine.publish resolves capability_revisions in this empty DB and stores undefined (serialized as null) capability snapshot entries; execute's capability lookup throws before a WAITING_AGENT checkpoint can receive the supplied fixture.
findings.impact: Every valid host_tool Mock case fails with an unrelated unknown-outcome diagnostic, blocking the required no-Key host-only test path and concealing the actual metadata gap.
findings.minimalFix: Snapshot the exact referenced capability revision metadata into the isolated DB before publishing; validate missing revisions explicitly. Carry only contract/Skill metadata needed for simulation and never endpoints or secrets. Publish non-null capability snapshots and distinguish a missing contract from missing case data.
tests: Official MCP test_generate/run/status on a host_tool workflow with a valid agent fixture reaches SUCCEEDED and provenance=synthetic, without external calls.
Same workflow without host fixture yields UNCOVERED/FIXTURE_MISSING.
Missing capability revision returns a typed missing/stale contract error, never TypeError/OUTCOME_UNKNOWN.
Host fixture output must obey the actual frozen schema from TEST-HOST-03 and cannot falsely assert actual host execution.

findings.title: test generation/run replays check mutable baselines before the idempotency ledger
findings.contract: Same owner + operation + idempotencyKey + request must return the existing accepted result without repeating work, including after a response is lost or another edit occurs.
findings.trigger: Call test.generate for draft r1; call test.run; then apply a metadata patch producing r2; repeat the exact original generate/run requests and keys.
findings.cause: generate's revision check and run's suite/baseline checks happen before repo.command can read a prior successful command.
findings.impact: A retry after a lost response cannot recover the accepted suite/test run once the draft or suite changes. Callers see an edit conflict or may create a new suite/run with a new key instead of recovering the existing operation.
findings.minimalFix: Keep current owner authorization and stateless DTO checks outside, but put mutable revision/baseline acceptance checks inside the first-execution command callback. Store/use the accepted immutable suite/case selection so queued job recovery never starts the newest suite on replay.
tests: Replay identical generate/run after draft edit returns original IDs and does not add suite/run records or execute cases again.
Replay after suite revision changes also recovers the old operation.
Same key with different body remains IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT; revoked/unauthorized owners cannot recover records.
Fresh new-key request against stale baseline still rejects.

pending.status: source-only candidate; not promoted to confirmed finding
pending.detail: workflow-testing mock adapter returns adaptMcpResult.value but bypasses Connectors.call environment cross-check, rowCount==rows.length check and raw result artifact attachment. A fixture could therefore appear green for output rejected by the runtime connector. Needs a focused repro and a clear simulation provenance policy before final severity.

undo always increments semantic revision, even undo of a move_nodes-only action; node config revert is shallow and rejects unrelated later config field edits. Verify UI expectations and exact conflict granularity before reporting.

Generator covers top-level input properties and boolean variants but does not inspect arbitrary/nested conditions or synthesize branch-driving tool/agent fixtures; branchCoverage can show true/false false without recording unreachable reasons. Compare against P0 generation/branch coverage requirements with a nonboolean branch repro.
